Words Upon The Wind

Jan 9, 2018 • Janice Cotcher

“What came first, the music or the misery? People worry about kids playing with guns, or watching violent videos, that some sort of culture of violence will take them over. Nobody worries about kids listening to thousands, literally thousands of songs about heartbreak, rejection, pain, misery and loss. Did I listen to pop music because I was miserable? Or was I miserable because I listened to pop music?” Rob, High Fidelity

What came first: the music or the misery? I don’t think that music specifically dictates my mood. I think, there are times, music reminds us of a moment, of misery, or of happiness. Other times our frame of mind leads us to seek out songs that feed our pain and wallowing. There was a time in my life where I had to stop listening to Chris Isaak because of the sorrow it caused. When you’re already in the depths of despair, you don’t want to dragged further into misery and suffering. Lately, I’ve been rediscovering the power of using music to lift my spirits. I used to make mixed CDs for friends going through hard times. I used to create playlists to “pump me up” or motivated myself. How did I get away from that? I became content to listen to music that allowed me to dwell on my anger and misery. There’s a time and place for that but also for music that cheers me up and lifts my spirits. I’m using music as medicine. “I let my music take me where my heart wants to go.” My heart wants to be light and open to new possibilities. My heart wants to be healed and escape loneliness. My heart wants to create art and listen to music and dance. I am changing, and music is helping me get there.
